title.zh: 卷82 列傳第47 南蠻
title.raw: 卷82 列傳第47 南蠻 Volume 82 Biographies 47: The Nanman

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 【序】南蠻雜類，與華人錯居，曰蜒，曰獽，曰俚，曰獠，曰㐌，俱無君長，隨山洞而居，古先所謂百越是也。

translations.literal: [Preface] The various sorts of southern barbarians, interspersed with Chinese, are called Yan, Xian, Li, Liao, and Yi; all lack rulers and chiefs, dwelling wherever mountain caves offer shelter—they are what the ancients called the Hundred Yue.
translations.idiomatic: [Preface] The miscellaneous peoples of the southern frontier live intermingled with the Chinese. They include the Yan, Xian, Li, Liao, and Yi. None of them have kings or chiefs; they take their dwellings in mountain caves. These are the peoples the ancients knew as the Hundred Yue.

sentences.zh: 其俗斷髮文身，好相攻討，浸以微弱，稍屬於中國，皆列為郡縣，同之齊人，不復詳載。

translations.literal: Their custom is to cut the hair and tattoo the body; they are fond of attacking one another. Gradually weakening, they gradually came under China; all were enrolled as commanderies and counties and treated like the people of Qi—no further detailed record is given here.
translations.idiomatic: They cut their hair short and tattoo their bodies, and they relish raiding one another. As they grew weaker, they were gradually absorbed into the Chinese sphere; all were organized as commanderies and counties and governed like ordinary subjects of the central lands. They are no longer described in detail below.

sentences.zh: 大業中，南荒朝貢者十餘國，其事迹多湮滅而無聞。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, more than a dozen states of the southern wilds came to court with tribute; most of their deeds have been lost and are unheard of.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign period more than a dozen southern realms sent tribute missions, but most of their histories have perished and their names are forgotten.

sentences.zh: 今所存錄，四國而已。

translations.literal: Of what is preserved in record today, there are only four states.
translations.idiomatic: Only four countries survive in the records that follow.

sentences.zh: 林邑林邑之先，因漢末交阯女子徵側之亂，內縣功曹子區連殺縣令，自號為王。

translations.literal: Linyi—The lineage of Linyi: because of the rebellion of the Jiaozhi woman Zheng Ce at the end of Han, the inner commandery clerk Qu Lian killed the magistrate and declared himself king.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi—The kingdom's origins lie in the turmoil at the end of the Han, when the Jiaozhi rebel Zheng Ce rose up. A clerk of the inner district named Qu Lian assassinated the magistrate and proclaimed himself king.

sentences.zh: 無子，其甥范熊代立，死，子逸立。

translations.literal: He had no son; his sister's son Fan Xiong succeeded him. When he died, his son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Lian left no son. His nephew Fan Xiong took the throne, and after Fan Xiong's death his son Yi became king.

sentences.zh: 日南人范文因亂為逸僕隸，遂教之築宮室，造器械。

translations.literal: A man of Rinan named Fan Wen became Yi's slave during the disorder, and went on to teach him how to build palaces and manufacture weapons.
translations.idiomatic: During the upheaval a Rinan native named Fan Wen entered Yi's service as a bondservant and taught him palace-building and the forging of arms.

sentences.zh: 逸甚信任，使文將兵，極得眾心。

translations.literal: Yi trusted him deeply and put Fan Wen in command of troops; Fan Wen won the utmost devotion of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yi relied on him completely, gave him command of the army, and Fan Wen won the wholehearted loyalty of the populace.

sentences.zh: 文因間其子弟，或奔或徙。

translations.literal: Fan Wen took the opportunity to drive away or disperse Yi's sons and younger kinsmen—some fled, some were relocated.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wen meanwhile uprooted Yi's sons and younger relatives, sending some into exile and displacing others.

sentences.zh: 及逸死，國無嗣，文自立為王。

translations.literal: When Yi died without an heir, Fan Wen declared himself king.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died leaving no successor, Fan Wen seized the throne for himself.

sentences.zh: 其後范佛為晉揚威將軍戴桓所破。

translations.literal: Later Fan Fo was defeated by Dai Huan, general of manifest authority under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Later his descendant Fan Fo was broken by Dai Huan, Jin's general of manifest authority.

sentences.zh: 宋交州刺史檀和之將兵擊之，深入其境。

translations.literal: Song's Inspector of Jiaozhou Tan Hezhi led troops to attack them and penetrated deep into their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, Inspector of Jiaozhou Tan Hezhi marched against them and drove deep into their lands.

sentences.zh: 至梁、陳，亦通使往來。

translations.literal: Through the Liang and Chen periods as well, envoys were exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang and Chen dynasties too they continued to send missions back and forth.

sentences.zh: 其國延袤數千里，土多香木金寶，物產大抵與交阯同。

translations.literal: The state stretched thousands of li; the soil bore fragrant woods, gold, and precious things; products were generally like those of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: The realm extended for thousands of li. Its soil produced fragrant timber, gold, and gems, and its commodities were much the same as Jiaozhi's.

sentences.zh: 以塼為城，蜃灰塗之，東向戶。

translations.literal: They used brick for city walls, coated them with clam-lime mortar, and doors faced east.
translations.idiomatic: City walls were built of brick and daubed with lime from shells; dwellings faced eastward.

sentences.zh: 尊官有二：其一曰西那婆帝，其二曰薩婆地歌。

translations.literal: Two exalted offices: one called Xina podi, the other Sapadi ge.
translations.idiomatic: There were two highest offices: one titled Xina Podi, the other Sapadi Ge.

sentences.zh: 其屬官三等：其一曰倫多姓，次歌倫致帝，次乙他伽蘭。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices in three grades: first Lun duo xing, next Gelun zhi di, next Yita galan.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate offices fell into three ranks: first Lun Duo Xing, next Ge Lun Zhi Di, next Yi Ta Galan.

sentences.zh: 外官分為二百餘部。

translations.literal: Outer offices were divided into more than two hundred departments.
translations.idiomatic: Field administration was split into more than two hundred bureaus.

sentences.zh: 其長官曰弗羅，次曰可輪，如牧宰之差也。

translations.literal: Their senior officials were called Fuluo, next Kelun—like the difference between prefect and magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Local heads were titled Fuluo, with Kelun beneath them—roughly the distinction between a prefect and a district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 王戴金花冠，形如章甫，衣朝霞布，珠璣瓔珞，足躡革履，時復錦袍。

translations.literal: The king wore a golden-flower crown shaped like a zhangfu cap, robe of zhaoxia cloth with pearl and jade pendants, leather shoes on his feet, and sometimes a brocade cloak.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a golden floral crown shaped like a formal cap, robes of dawn-glow silk hung with pearls and jade, leather sandals on his feet, and on occasion a brocade mantle.

sentences.zh: 良家子侍衞者二百許人，皆執金裝刀。

translations.literal: About two hundred sons of good families served as guards, all holding gilt swords.
translations.idiomatic: Some two hundred young men of distinguished houses formed his guard, each bearing a gilded blade.

sentences.zh: 有弓、箭、刀、槊，以竹為弩，傅毒於矢。

translations.literal: They had bows, arrows, knives, and spears; crossbows were of bamboo, arrows poisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Their armament included bows, arrows, knives, and spears; crossbows were fashioned from bamboo and their bolt tips were smeared with poison.

sentences.zh: 樂有琴、笛、琵琶、五絃，頗與中國同。

translations.literal: Music had qin, di, pipa, and five-string lute, much like China's.
translations.idiomatic: Musical instruments included the zither, flute, pipa, and five-string lute—largely the same as in China.

sentences.zh: 每擊鼓以警眾，吹蠡以即戎。

translations.literal: Whenever they beat drums to alert the multitude, they blew conches to summon warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Drums sounded to rally the people; conch horns blasted to call men to arms.

sentences.zh: 其人深目高鼻，髮拳色黑。

translations.literal: The people had deep-set eyes and high noses, curly black hair.
translations.idiomatic: Its people had deep-set eyes, prominent noses, and tight curls of black hair.

sentences.zh: 俗皆徒跣，以幅布纏身。

translations.literal: Customarily they went barefoot, wrapping the body in strips of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they went barefoot and wrapped their bodies in bolt cloth.

sentences.zh: 冬月衣袍。

translations.literal: In winter months they wore robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the cold season they wore gowns.

sentences.zh: 婦人椎髻。

translations.literal: Women wore hair in topknots.
translations.idiomatic: Women dressed their hair in topknots.

sentences.zh: 施椰葉席。

translations.literal: They spread coconut-palm leaf mats.
translations.idiomatic: They laid out mats woven from coconut fronds.

sentences.zh: 每有婚媾，令媒者齎金銀釧、酒二壺、魚數頭至女家。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a marriage, they sent a matchmaker bearing gold and silver bracelets, two jars of wine, and several fish to the bride's house.
translations.idiomatic: For each betrothal a go-between carried gold and silver bangles, two jars of wine, and several fish to the bride's family.

sentences.zh: 於是擇日，夫家會親賓，歌儛相對。

translations.literal: Thus on the chosen day the groom's kin assembled guests; songs and dances faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the groom's household gathered kin and guests in reciprocal song and dance.

sentences.zh: 女家請一婆羅門，送女至男家，壻盥手，因牽女授之。

translations.literal: The bride's family invited a brahmin who escorted the bride to the groom's house; the groom washed his hands and received her by the hand.
translations.idiomatic: The bride's people summoned a Brahmin to escort her to the groom's home, where the bridegroom washed his hands and took her hand in the wedding rite.

sentences.zh: 王死七日而葬，有官者三日，庶人一日。

translations.literal: When the king died he was buried after seven days; officials after three days; commoners after one day.
translations.idiomatic: Kings were interred seven days after death, officials after three days, commoners after one.

sentences.zh: 皆以函盛屍，鼓儛導從，輿至水次，積薪焚之。

translations.literal: All placed the corpse in a coffin; with drum music and dancing leading, they bore it to the water's edge and heaped firewood to burn it.
translations.idiomatic: Every corpse was placed in a chest, led to the waterside to the beat of drums and dancers, and burned on a pyre.

sentences.zh: 收其餘骨，王則內金甖中，沉之於海；

translations.literal: They gathered the remaining bones; for the king they placed them in a gold urn and sank it in the sea;
translations.idiomatic: After cremation the bones were collected: a king's remains went into a golden jar and were sunk in the sea;

sentences.zh: 有官者以銅甖，沉之於海口；

translations.literal: for officials a bronze urn, sunk at the sea mouth;
translations.idiomatic: officials' into a bronze jar and lowered at the estuary;

sentences.zh: 庶人以瓦，送之於江。

translations.literal: commoners into pottery, sent down the river.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners' remains were placed in earthenware vessels and committed to the river.

sentences.zh: 男女皆截髮，隨喪至水次，盡哀而止，歸則不哭。

translations.literal: Men and women all cut their hair; they followed the bier to the water, weeping until grief ended, and did not weep again on returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike cropped their hair and followed the funeral train to the water, mourning until they could mourn no more, and did not weep once they returned home.

sentences.zh: 每七日，然香散花，復哭，盡哀而止，盡七七而罷，至百日、三年，亦如之。

translations.literal: Every seven days they burned incense and scattered flowers and wept again until grief ended; this continued through seven sevens, and at one hundred days and three years likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Every seventh day they burned incense, strewed flowers, and mourned anew until sorrow was spent—forty-nine days in all—with the same observances at the hundredth day and the third anniversary.

sentences.zh: 人皆奉佛，文字同於天竺。

translations.literal: All revered the Buddha; their writing was the same as India's.
translations.idiomatic: The people were Buddhist devotees, and their script was the same as that of India.

sentences.zh: 高祖既平陳，乃遣使獻方物，其後朝貢遂絕。

translations.literal: After Gaozu pacified Chen, he sent envoys to present local products; thereafter tribute missions ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozu conquered Chen, Linyi sent envoys bearing native products, but tributary missions soon ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，羣臣言林邑多奇寶者。

translations.literal: When the realm was at peace, officials said Linyi possessed many rare treasures.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire at peace, court officials declared that Linyi held countless exotic treasures.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，上遣大將軍劉方為驩州道行軍總管，率欽州刺史甯長真、驩州刺史李暈、開府秦雄步騎萬餘及犯罪者數千人擊之。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou, the emperor dispatched Grand General Liu Fang as commander-in-chief of the Huanzhou route army, leading Prefect of Qin Zhou Ning Changzhen, Prefect of Huan Zhou Li Yun, Colonel Qin Xiong with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry plus several thousand convicted men to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Renshou era the emperor appointed Grand General Liu Fang commander of the Huanzhou expeditionary force. Liu Fang marched with Prefect of Qinzhou Ning Changzhen, Prefect of Huanzhou Li Yun, colonel Qin Xiong, over ten thousand foot and horse soldiers, and several thousand penal conscripts to strike Linyi.

sentences.zh: 其王梵志率其徒乘巨象而戰，方軍不利。

translations.literal: King Fan Zhi led his troops mounted on huge elephants to battle; Fang's army fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: King Fan Zhi arrayed his warriors atop great elephants, and Liu Fang's forces suffered at first.

sentences.zh: 方於是多掘小坑，草覆其上，因以兵挑之。

translations.literal: Fang then had many small pits dug, covered with grass, and provoked the enemy with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang ordered countless shallow pits dug, masked with turf, and baited the enemy with skirmishers.

sentences.zh: 梵志悉眾而陣，方與戰，偽北，梵志逐之，至坑所，其眾多陷，轉相驚駭，軍遂亂。

translations.literal: Fan Zhi marshaled his entire host in formation; Fang engaged and feigned retreat; Fan Zhi pursued to the pits, many men fell in, panic spread, and the army fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi drew up his full army; Liu Fang fought, then feigned defeat. Fan Zhi gave chase; when his men reached the pits masses stumbled in, terror rippled through the ranks, and the host collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 方縱兵擊之，大破之。

translations.literal: Fang let his troops strike and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang unleashed his troops and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 頻戰輒敗，遂棄城而走。

translations.literal: Repeated battles they lost; finally they abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Battle after battle ended in defeat until they abandoned their capital and fled.

sentences.zh: 方入其都，獲其廟主十八枚，皆鑄金為之，蓋其有國十八葉矣。

translations.literal: Fang entered their capital and seized eighteen spirit tablets of their temple, all cast in gold—for their kingdom had endured eighteen generations.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang entered the capital and took eighteen ancestral spirit tablets, all cast in gold—proof that the dynasty had ruled for eighteen generations.

sentences.zh: 方班師，梵志復其故地，遣使謝罪，於是朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: As Fang withdrew, Fan Zhi recovered his former territory and sent envoys to apologize; thereafter tribute never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Fang withdrew, Fan Zhi regained his old lands and dispatched envoys to sue for pardon; from then on tribute flowed without interruption.

sentences.zh: 赤土赤土國，扶南之別種也。

translations.literal: Chitu—The state of Red Earth was a separate branch of Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Chitu (Red Earth)—This realm was an offshoot of Funan.

sentences.zh: 在南海中，水行百餘日而達所都。

translations.literal: It lay in the southern sea; a voyage of more than a hundred days reached its capital.
translations.idiomatic: It stood amid the southern oceans; reaching its capital required more than a hundred days at sea.

sentences.zh: 土色多赤，因以為號。

translations.literal: Much of the soil was red, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: The earth was predominantly red, which gave the country its name.

sentences.zh: 東波羅剌國，西婆羅娑國，南訶羅旦國，北拒大海，地方數千里。

translations.literal: East lay Boluola state, west Parasa state, south Haradanta state, north the great sea; the territory measured several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: To the east lay Boluola, to the west Parasa, to the south Haradanta, and to the north the open ocean; the domain stretched several thousand li.

sentences.zh: 其王姓瞿曇氏，名利富多塞，不知有國近遠。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Gautama; his name Lifuduosai; he knew neither how near nor how far other realms might be.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Gautama clan and was named Lifuduosai; he had no notion of other countries' proximity or distance.

sentences.zh: 稱其父釋王位出家為道，傳位於利富多塞，在位十六年矣。

translations.literal: He said his father had relinquished the kingship to follow the Way and transmitted the throne to Lifuduosai, who had reigned sixteen years.
translations.idiomatic: He explained that his father had abdicated to pursue the Buddhist path and passed the throne to Lifuduosai, who had already ruled sixteen years.

sentences.zh: 有三妻，並鄰國王之女也。

translations.literal: He had three consorts, all daughters of neighboring kings.
translations.idiomatic: He kept three wives, each a princess from a neighboring realm.

sentences.zh: 居僧祗城，有門三重，相去各百許步。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the monk's quarter city; the gates were triple, each gate about a hundred paces apart.
translations.idiomatic: His residence was the Sangha Capital, ringed by three gates spaced roughly a hundred paces apart.

sentences.zh: 每門圖畫飛仙、仙人、菩薩之像，縣金花鈴毦，婦女數十人，或奏樂，或捧金花。

translations.literal: At each gate were painted flying immortals, transcendent beings, and bodhisattvas; golden-flower bells and tassels hung; dozens of women either played music or bore golden flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Every gate was painted with flying immortals, perfected beings, and bodhisattvas; golden floral bells and pennants hung overhead while dozens of women played music or carried golden blossoms.

sentences.zh: 又飾四婦人，容飾如佛塔邊金剛力士之狀，夾門而立。

translations.literal: Four women were adorned in the manner of the vajra guardians beside a stupa, standing flanking the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Four attendants were costumed like the diamond guardians at a pagoda's base and stood on either side of the gate.

sentences.zh: 門外者持兵仗，門內者執白佛。

translations.literal: Those outside the gate bore weapons; those inside bore white Buddhist banners.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the gate stood armed guards; inside, attendants bearing white Buddhist standards.

sentences.zh: 夾道垂素網，綴花。

translations.literal: Along the roadway hung white silk nets strung with flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The avenue was draped with white silk nets adorned with blossoms.

sentences.zh: 王宮諸屋悉是重閣，北戶，北面而坐。

translations.literal: All palace buildings were storied structures with north-facing doors; he sat facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Every structure in the royal quarter was multi-storied, its doors opening to the north, and the king sat facing northward.

sentences.zh: 坐三重之榻。

translations.literal: He sat on a triple-layered couch.
translations.idiomatic: He occupied a couch stacked three tiers high.

sentences.zh: 衣朝霞布，冠金花冠，垂雜寶瓔珞。

translations.literal: He wore dawn-glow silk robes, a golden floral crown, and pendants of assorted gems.
translations.idiomatic: Dawn-glow silk clothed him; a golden floral crown crowned him; strings of assorted gems hung from his neck.

sentences.zh: 四女子立侍，左右兵衞百餘人。

translations.literal: Four women stood in attendance; over a hundred armed guards flanked him left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Four women waited at his side while more than a hundred armed attendants guarded him.

sentences.zh: 王榻後作一木龕，以金銀五香木雜鈿之。

translations.literal: Behind the royal couch stood a wooden shrine inlaid with gold, silver, and assorted fragrant woods.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the royal couch rose a wooden shrine inlaid with gold, silver, and fragrant hardwoods.

sentences.zh: 龕後懸一金光焰，夾榻又樹二金鏡，鏡前並陳金甕，甕前各有金香爐。

translations.literal: Behind the shrine hung a golden flame-banner; flanking the couch stood two golden mirrors; before the mirrors golden jars, and before each jar a golden incense burner.
translations.idiomatic: A golden flame-banner hung behind the shrine; a pair of golden mirrors flanked the couch; golden vessels stood before the mirrors, each paired with a golden censer.

sentences.zh: 當前置一金伏牛，牛前樹壹寶蓋，蓋左右皆有寶扇。

translations.literal: In front was placed a golden recumbent ox; before the ox stood a single jeweled canopy, with jeweled fans on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Before him stood a golden recumbent ox; before the ox rose one jeweled canopy flanked by jeweled fans.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門等數百人，東西重行，相向而坐。

translations.literal: Several hundred brahmins sat in double rows east and west, facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Brahmins sat in facing ranks, east and west.

sentences.zh: 其官有薩陀迦羅一人，陀拏達义二人，迦利蜜迦三人，共掌政事；

translations.literal: Officials: one Saduogaluo, two Tanaodayi, three Kalimijia—together they managed government affairs;
translations.idiomatic: His chief ministers were one Saduogaluo, two Tanaodayi, and three Kalimijia, who jointly governed civil affairs;

sentences.zh: 俱羅末帝一人，掌刑法。

translations.literal: one Juluomodi in charge of penal law.
translations.idiomatic: one Juluomodi who oversaw criminal law.

sentences.zh: 每城置那邪迦一人，鉢帝十人。

translations.literal: In each city one Nayage and ten Bodai were installed.
translations.idiomatic: Each city had one Nayage and ten Bodai officers.

sentences.zh: 其俗等皆穿耳剪髮，無跪拜之禮。

translations.literal: Their custom alike: all pierced ears and cut hair; there was no bowing or kneeling ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Custom required everyone to pierce the ears and crop the hair; prostration and kneeling were unknown.

sentences.zh: 以香油塗身。

translations.literal: They smeared fragrant oil on the body.
translations.idiomatic: They anointed their bodies with perfumed oil.

sentences.zh: 其俗敬佛，尤重婆羅門。

translations.literal: The people reverenced the Buddha and especially honored brahmins.
translations.idiomatic: They were devout Buddhists who held Brahmins in the highest esteem.

sentences.zh: 婦人作髻於項後。

translations.literal: Women arranged their hair in buns at the nape.
translations.idiomatic: Women dressed their hair in coils at the nape of the neck.

sentences.zh: 男女通以朝霞、朝雲雜色布為衣。

translations.literal: Men and women alike wore dawn-glow and dawn-cloud patterned cloth for garments.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike dressed in dawn-glow and dawn-cloud silks of mixed colors.

sentences.zh: 豪富之室，恣意華靡，唯金鎖非王賜不得服用。

translations.literal: In wealthy households they indulged in splendor at will; only golden chains could not be worn unless bestowed by the king.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households dressed as lavishly as they pleased, yet golden chains could be worn only when the king granted them.

sentences.zh: 每婚嫁，擇吉日，女家先期五日，作樂飲酒，父執女手以授壻，七日乃配焉。

translations.literal: For each marriage they chose an auspicious day; the bride's family five days beforehand made music and drank wine; the father took his daughter's hand and gave her to the groom; after seven days the union was consummated.
translations.idiomatic: Weddings were timed to auspicious days. Five days before, the bride's family feasted with music and wine; the father placed his daughter's hand in the bridegroom's; only after seven days was the marriage completed.

sentences.zh: 既娶則分財別居，唯幼子與父同居。

translations.literal: After marriage property was divided and they lived apart; only the youngest son remained with the father.
translations.idiomatic: After marriage brothers divided the household estates and lived separately; only the youngest son stayed with his father.

sentences.zh: 父母兄弟死則剔髮素服，就水上構竹木為棚，棚內積薪，以屍置上。

translations.literal: When parents or brothers died they shaved their heads and wore plain mourning, built bamboo-and-wood platforms over the water, heaped firewood inside, and placed the corpse upon it.
translations.idiomatic: On the death of parents or siblings they shaved their heads, wore undyed mourning garb, built bamboo platforms on the water, piled fuel within, and laid the corpse on top.

sentences.zh: 燒香建幡，吹蠡擊鼓以送之，縱火焚薪，遂落於水。

translations.literal: They burned incense and raised banners, blew conches and beat drums to send them off, set the firewood ablaze, and the remains fell into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Incense burned, banners rose, conches and drums sounded for the send-off; the pyre was lit and the body fell into the water.

sentences.zh: 貴賤皆同。

translations.literal: Noble and common alike were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Rich and poor observed the same rite.

sentences.zh: 唯國王燒訖，收灰貯以金瓶，藏於廟屋。

translations.literal: Only when the king's burning was finished were the ashes gathered into a gold bottle and stored in the temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Only for the king were the ashes collected afterward into a golden flask and kept in the temple.

sentences.zh: 冬夏常溫，雨多霽少，種植無時，特宜稻、穄、白豆、黑麻，自餘物產多同於交阯。

translations.literal: Winter and summer were always warm; rain was frequent and clear weather rare; planting had no fixed season; rice, millet, white beans, and black sesame were especially suitable; remaining products were mostly like Jiaozhi's.
translations.idiomatic: The climate stayed warm year-round, with much rain and little sunshine. Crops could be planted at any season; rice, millet, white beans, and black sesame thrived especially, while other produce largely matched Jiaozhi's.

sentences.zh: 以甘蔗作酒，雜以紫瓜根。

translations.literal: They made wine from sugarcane mixed with purple melon root.
translations.idiomatic: They fermented liquor from sugarcane blended with purple gourd root.

sentences.zh: 酒色黃赤，味亦香美。

translations.literal: The wine's color was yellow-red and the taste fragrant and fine.
translations.idiomatic: The brew ran yellow-red and tasted fragrant and fine.

sentences.zh: 亦名椰漿為酒。

translations.literal: They also called coconut sap wine.
translations.idiomatic: Coconut sap served as another kind of wine.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，募能通絕域者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne he recruited men able to reach the farthest realms.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang took the throne he sought out men capable of crossing to the remotest lands.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，屯田主事常駿、虞部主事王君政等請使赤土。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, agricultural officer Chang Jun and palace supplies officer Wang Junzheng and others requested mission to Chitu.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 3, agricultural intendant Chang Jun and supplies officer Wang Junzheng petitioned to go to Chitu.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜駿等帛各百匹，時服一襲而遣。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed on Jun and the others one hundred bolts of silk each plus one set of court dress and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, granted each of them a hundred bolts of silk and a suit of court robes, and dispatched them.

sentences.zh: 齎物五千段，以賜赤土王。

translations.literal: They carried five thousand lengths of goods to bestow on the king of Chitu.
translations.idiomatic: They bore five thousand bolts of goods as gifts for the king of Red Earth.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，駿等自南海郡乘舟，晝夜二旬，每值便風。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month Jun and the others embarked from Nanhai commandery; day and night for twenty days, whenever favoring winds blew.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year they set sail from Nanhai Commandery and, with fair winds whenever they arose, made the passage in twenty days and nights.

sentences.zh: 至焦石山而過，東南泊陵伽鉢拔多洲，西與林邑相對，上有神祠焉。

translations.literal: They passed Jiaoshi Mountain, then moored southeast at Lingjiaboduo Isle, which lay opposite Linyi to the west and held a spirit shrine.
translations.idiomatic: They passed Jiaoshi Mountain and anchored southeast at Lingjiaboduo Island, west of which lay Linyi and on which stood a spirit shrine.

sentences.zh: 又南行，至師子石，自是島嶼連接。

translations.literal: Sailing south again they reached Shizi Rock; from there islands linked one to the next.
translations.idiomatic: Continuing south they came to Lion Rock, beyond which islands stretched in an unbroken chain.

sentences.zh: 又行二三日，西望見狼牙須國之山，於是南達雞籠島，至於赤土之界。

translations.literal: After two or three more days they saw to the west the mountains of Langyaxu state; then south to Jilong Island, reaching the borders of Chitu.
translations.idiomatic: Two or three days farther on they sighted westward the mountains of Langyaxu, then sailed south to Jilong Island and entered Red Earth's territory.

sentences.zh: 其王遣婆羅門鳩摩羅以舶三十艘來迎，吹蠡擊鼓，以樂隋使，進金鎖以纜駿船。

translations.literal: The king sent the brahmin Jumoluo with thirty ships to welcome them; conches and drums sounded; music honored the Sui envoys; golden chains were presented to moor Jun's vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent the Brahmin Jumoluo with thirty ships to meet them. Conches blared and drums thundered in salute to the Sui mission, and golden chains were offered to berth Chang Jun's ship.

sentences.zh: 月餘，至其都，王遣其子那邪迦請與駿等禮見。

translations.literal: After more than a month they reached the capital; the king sent his son Nayage to request an audience with Jun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month they arrived at the capital, where the king sent his son Nayage to invite Chang Jun and his party to an audience.

sentences.zh: 先遣人送金盤，貯香花并鏡鑷，金合二枚，貯香油，金瓶八枚，貯香水，白疊布四條，以擬供使者盥洗。

translations.literal: First they sent men bringing a golden platter holding fragrant flowers together with mirror tweezers, two golden boxes holding fragrant oil, eight golden bottles holding scented water, and four bolts of white layered cloth for the envoys' ablutions.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys went ahead with a golden tray of fragrant blossoms, mirror and tweezers, two golden boxes of scented oil, eight golden flasks of perfumed water, and four bolts of white gauze for the diplomats' ceremonial washing.

sentences.zh: 其日未時，那邪迦又將象二頭，持孔雀蓋以迎使人，并致金花、金盤以藉詔函。

translations.literal: That day at the wei hour Nayage again led two elephants, holding a peacock canopy to welcome the envoys, and also presented golden flowers and a golden platter to cushion the imperial letter case.
translations.idiomatic: That afternoon Nayage returned with two elephants and a peacock-feather canopy to greet the envoys, and sent golden blossoms and a golden tray to bear the imperial letter case.

sentences.zh: 男女百人奏蠡鼓，婆羅門二人導路，至王宮。

translations.literal: A hundred men and women played conch drums; two brahmins guided the way to the royal palace.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred men and women beat conch drums while two Brahmins led the procession to the palace.

sentences.zh: 駿等奉詔書上閣，王以下皆坐。

translations.literal: Jun and the others presented the imperial letter on the upper hall; the king and all below sat.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jun and his party presented the edict in the upper hall; the king and his court were seated.

sentences.zh: 宣詔訖，引駿等坐，奏天竺樂。

translations.literal: When the edict had been proclaimed, they led Jun and the others to seats and performed Indian music.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict was read they seated Chang Jun and his companions and performed music from India.

sentences.zh: 事畢，駿等還館，又遣婆羅門就館送食，以草葉為盤，其大方丈。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished Jun and the others returned to the lodge; brahmins were again sent to the lodge with food, using grass leaves as platters about a zhang square.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony ended the envoys returned to their quarters, where Brahmins brought food on leaf platters each about ten feet square.

sentences.zh: 因謂駿曰：「今是大國中人，非復赤土國矣。

translations.literal: They then said to Jun: "You are now men of a great state, no longer of the state of Red Earth.
translations.idiomatic: They told Chang Jun, "You are guests of a great empire now, no longer mere visitors from Red Earth.

sentences.zh: 飲食疎薄，願為大國意而食之。」

translations.literal: The food is coarse and thin; we wish you to eat with the great state's intent in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Our fare is humble; please accept it in the spirit of your great realm.

sentences.zh: 後數日，請駿等入宴，儀衞導從如初見之禮。

translations.literal: Several days later they invited Jun and the others to a banquet; guards and attendants escorted them with the same ceremony as at the first audience.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later they invited the envoys to a banquet with the same guard and ceremonial escort as at the first audience.

sentences.zh: 王前設兩牀，牀上并設草葉盤，方一丈五尺，上有黃白紫赤四色之餅，牛、羊、魚、鼈、猪、蝳蝐之肉百餘品。

translations.literal: Before the king two couches were set; on each couch grass-leaf platters fifteen chi square, bearing yellow, white, purple, and red cakes, and more than a hundred kinds of beef, mutton, fish, turtle, pork, and oyster meat.
translations.idiomatic: Before the king stood two couches, each bearing leaf platters fifteen feet square piled with yellow, white, purple, and red cakes and more than a hundred dishes of beef, mutton, fish, turtle, pork, and shellfish.

sentences.zh: 延駿升牀，從者坐於地席，各以金鍾置酒，女樂迭奏，禮遺甚厚。

translations.literal: They invited Jun up onto the couch; attendants sat on ground mats, each with a golden goblet set with wine; female musicians played in turn; gifts and courtesy were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jun was invited onto the couch while his attendants sat on mats below, each with a golden cup of wine; female musicians played in succession, and the hospitality was lavish.

sentences.zh: 尋遣那邪迦隨駿貢方物，并獻金芙蓉冠、龍腦香。

translations.literal: Soon they sent Nayage to accompany Jun in presenting local products, and also offered a golden lotus crown and dragon-brain incense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Nayage was sent to accompany Chang Jun home with tribute goods, including a golden lotus crown and dragon-brain camphor.

sentences.zh: 以鑄金為多羅葉，隱起成文以為表，金函封之，令婆羅門以香花奏蠡鼓而送之。

translations.literal: They cast gold into bodhi-leaf form with raised inscriptions as a memorial, sealed it in a golden case, and had brahmins with fragrant flowers playing conch drums to send them off.
translations.idiomatic: They cast gold into bodhi-leaf plaques inscribed with raised text as a formal tribute document, sealed it in a golden casket, and sent Brahmins with flowers and conch drums to see the mission off.

sentences.zh: 既入海，見綠魚羣飛水上。

translations.literal: Once they entered the sea they saw green fish flying in groups above the water.
translations.idiomatic: Once at sea they saw shoals of green fish skimming the surface.

sentences.zh: 浮海十餘日，至林邑東南，並山而行。

translations.literal: They floated on the sea more than ten days, reaching southeast of Linyi, sailing along the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days at sea they reached the southeast of Linyi and coasted along the mountains.

sentences.zh: 其海水闊千餘步，色黃氣腥，舟行一日不絕，云是大魚糞也。

translations.literal: The seawater there was more than a thousand paces wide, yellow in color and foul-smelling; a boat could sail a full day without passing through it—they said it was the excrement of great fish.
translations.idiomatic: The water stretched more than a thousand paces across, yellow and foul; a ship could sail a full day without leaving it, which they said was the droppings of enormous fish.

sentences.zh: 循海北岸，達于交阯。

translations.literal: Following the northern shore of the sea, they reached Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: They followed the northern coast until they reached Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 駿以六年春與那邪迦於弘農謁，帝大悅，賜駿等物二百段，俱授秉義尉，那邪迦等官賞各有差。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year Jun and Nayage had audience at Hongnong; the emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed on Jun and the others two hundred lengths of goods, all appointed Bearer of Righteousness Commandant, and Nayage and the others received official rewards in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Daye year 6 Chang Jun and Nayage were received at Hongnong. The emperor was delighted, granted two hundred lengths of goods to the envoys, appointed them all Bearer of Righteousness Commandants, and rewarded Nayage and his party with offices of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 真臘真臘國，在林邑西南，本扶南之屬國也。

translations.literal: Zhenla—The state of Zhenla lay southwest of Linyi; it was originally a subject state of Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenla—This kingdom lay southwest of Linyi and had originally been a dependency of Funan.

sentences.zh: 去日南郡舟行六十日，而南接車渠國，西有朱江國。

translations.literal: From Rinan commandery sixty days by boat; south it bordered Chequ state, west lay Zhujiang state.
translations.idiomatic: It lay sixty days' sail from Rinan Commandery; Chequ bordered it to the south and Zhujiang to the west.

sentences.zh: 其王姓剎利氏，名質多斯那。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Kshatriya; his name Zhiduosina.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Kshatriya clan and was named Zhiduosina.

sentences.zh: 自其祖漸已強盛，至質多斯那，遂兼扶南而有之。

translations.literal: From his ancestors they had gradually grown strong; by Zhiduosina's time they had annexed Funan and possessed it.
translations.idiomatic: His line had grown steadily stronger since his forebears' day; under Zhiduosina they annexed Funan outright.

sentences.zh: 死，子伊奢那先代立。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Yishena succeeded in his place.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son Yishena ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 居伊奢那城，郭下二萬餘家。

translations.literal: He dwelt in Yishena city; outside the walls were more than twenty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled from Yishena City, which held more than twenty thousand households within its outer walls.

sentences.zh: 城中有一大堂，是王聽政之所。

translations.literal: Within the city was one great hall, the place where the king heard government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A great hall in the city served as the seat of royal government.

sentences.zh: 總大城三十，城有數千家，各有部帥，官名與林邑同。

translations.literal: In all thirty great cities, each with several thousand households, each with its own commander; official titles were the same as Linyi's.
translations.idiomatic: The realm comprised thirty major cities of several thousand households each, each with its own commander; official titles matched those of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 其王三日一聽朝，坐五香七寶牀，上施寶帳。

translations.literal: The king held court every three days, seated on a five-fragrance seven-treasure couch with a jeweled canopy above.
translations.idiomatic: The king held audience every third day, seated on a couch of five aromatics and seven treasures beneath a jeweled canopy.

sentences.zh: 其帳以文木為竿，象牙、金鈿為壁，狀如小屋，懸金光焰，有同於赤土。

translations.literal: The canopy used patterned wood for poles, ivory and gold inlay for walls, shaped like a small house, with a golden flame-banner suspended—much like Red Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy's poles were carved hardwood, its walls ivory and gold inlay shaped like a small pavilion, with a golden flame-banner hanging above—much as in Red Earth.

sentences.zh: 前有金香鑪，二人侍側。

translations.literal: Before it stood a golden incense burner; two attendants waited at the side.
translations.idiomatic: A golden censer stood before him with two attendants at his side.

sentences.zh: 王着朝霞古貝，瞞絡腰腹，下垂至脛，頭戴金寶花冠，被真珠瓔珞，足履革屣，耳懸金璫。

translations.literal: The king wore dawn-glow ancient shell cloth, a wrap around waist and belly hanging to the shins, a golden jeweled floral crown on his head, true-pearl pendants on his body, leather sandals on his feet, golden earrings suspended from his ears.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore dawn-glow cotton, a wrap about waist and hips falling to the shins, a golden floral crown studded with gems, strings of pearls, leather sandals, and golden earrings.

sentences.zh: 常服白疊，以象牙為屩。

translations.literal: For ordinary dress he wore white layered cloth and ivory for shoes.
translations.idiomatic: For everyday dress he wore white gauze and ivory sandals.

sentences.zh: 若露髮，則不加瓔珞。

translations.literal: If his hair was uncovered, he did not add the pearl pendants.
translations.idiomatic: When his hair was uncovered he wore no pearl necklaces.

sentences.zh: 臣人服製，大抵相類。

translations.literal: Subjects' dress and regulations were generally similar.
translations.idiomatic: His subjects' dress followed much the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 有五大臣，一曰孤落支，二曰高相憑，三曰婆何多陵，四曰舍摩陵，五曰髯多婁，及諸小臣。

translations.literal: There were five great ministers: first Guluo zhi, second Gaoxiang ping, third Poheduo ling, fourth Shemo ling, fifth Randuo lou, and various lesser ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Five great ministers—Guluo Zhi, Gaoxiang Ping, Poheduo Ling, Shemo Ling, and Randuo Lou—headed a host of lesser officials.

sentences.zh: 朝於王者，輒以階下三稽首。

translations.literal: Those attending audience with the king always performed three prostrations below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers approaching the throne always kowtowed three times at the foot of the steps.

sentences.zh: 王喚上階，則跪，以兩手抱膊，遶王環坐。

translations.literal: When the king summoned them up the steps they knelt, embraced their arms with both hands, and sat in a circle around the king.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned up the steps they knelt, clasped their arms, and sat in a ring around the king.

sentences.zh: 議政事訖，跪伏而去。

translations.literal: When government affairs had been discussed they knelt prostrate and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When business was finished they prostrated themselves and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 階庭門閣，侍衞有千餘人，被甲持仗。

translations.literal: On the steps, courtyard, gates, and pavilions, guards numbered more than a thousand, armored and bearing weapons.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand armored guards with weapons stood on the steps, in the courtyard, and at the gates.

sentences.zh: 其國與參半、朱江二國和親，數與林邑、陀桓二國戰爭。

translations.literal: The state was allied by marriage with Canban and Zhujiang; it frequently warred with Linyi and Tuohuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenla was allied by marriage with Canban and Zhujiang but fought repeatedly with Linyi and Tuohuan.

sentences.zh: 其人行止皆持甲仗，若有征伐，因而用之。

translations.literal: Its people in going about always carried armor and weapons; if there was campaigning, they used them accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Its people went about always armed; when war arose they were ready at once.

sentences.zh: 其俗非王正妻子，不得為嗣。

translations.literal: By their custom only the king's principal wife's son could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: By custom only a son of the king's principal wife could inherit the throne.

sentences.zh: 王初立之日，所有兄弟並刑殘之，或去一指，或劓其鼻，別處供給，不得仕進。

translations.literal: On the day the king first took the throne, all his brothers were mutilated by punishment—some lost a finger, some had their noses cut off—settled elsewhere with provisions, and could not enter office.
translations.idiomatic: On the day a new king was enthroned every brother was mutilated—one finger cut off or the nose severed—then settled elsewhere on an allowance and barred from office forever.

sentences.zh: 人形小而色黑。

translations.literal: People were small in stature and dark in color.
translations.idiomatic: The people were short and dark-skinned.

sentences.zh: 婦人亦有白者。

translations.literal: Among women some were also fair-skinned.
translations.idiomatic: Some women were fair-skinned as well.

sentences.zh: 悉拳髮垂耳，性氣捷勁。

translations.literal: All had curly hair hanging to the ears; their nature was quick and vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: All wore their curly hair to the ears; they were quick-tempered and vigorous by nature.

sentences.zh: 居處器物頗類赤土。

translations.literal: Dwellings and utensils were quite like Red Earth's.
translations.idiomatic: Their dwellings and furnishings resembled those of Red Earth.

sentences.zh: 以右手為淨，左手為穢。

translations.literal: The right hand was considered pure, the left hand defiled.
translations.idiomatic: The right hand was pure, the left hand unclean.

sentences.zh: 每旦澡洗，以楊枝淨齒，讀誦經呪。

translations.literal: Every dawn they bathed and washed, cleaned teeth with willow branches, and recited sutras and spells.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning they bathed, cleaned their teeth with willow twigs, and chanted sutras and spells.

sentences.zh: 又澡洒乃食，食罷還用楊枝淨齒，又讀經呪。

translations.literal: Again they bathed and sprinkled before eating; after eating they again used willow branches to clean teeth and again recited sutras and spells.
translations.idiomatic: They bathed again before eating; after the meal they once more cleaned their teeth with willow twigs and chanted sutras.

sentences.zh: 飲食多蘇酪、沙糖、秔粟、米餅。

translations.literal: Food and drink were mostly butter, rock sugar, husked millet, and rice cakes.
translations.idiomatic: Their diet consisted chiefly of butter, rock sugar, husked grain, and rice cakes.

sentences.zh: 欲食之時，先取雜肉羹與餅相和，手擩而食。

translations.literal: When they wished to eat, they first took assorted meat broth mixed with cakes and ate by kneading with the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Before eating they mixed assorted meat broth with cakes and ate by hand, kneading the food together.

sentences.zh: 娶妻者，唯送衣一具，擇日遣媒人迎婦。

translations.literal: One who took a wife sent only one set of clothing; on a chosen day a matchmaker was sent to fetch the bride.
translations.idiomatic: A suitor sent only one suit of clothing; on an auspicious day a matchmaker was dispatched to bring home the bride.

sentences.zh: 男女二家各八日不出，晝夜燃燈不息。

translations.literal: The bride's and groom's families each stayed indoors eight days, lamps burning day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Both families kept to their houses for eight days while lamps burned day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 男婚禮畢，即與父母分財別居。

translations.literal: When the man's wedding rites were finished he immediately divided property with his parents and lived apart.
translations.idiomatic: Once the wedding rites were complete the groom divided the family property and set up his own household.

sentences.zh: 父母死，小兒未婚者，以餘財與之。

translations.literal: When parents died, younger sons who were unmarried received the remaining wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When parents died, any unmarried younger son received the remaining estate.

sentences.zh: 若婚畢，財物入官。

translations.literal: If the marriage was already completed, the property went to the state.
translations.idiomatic: If he was already married, the property reverted to the crown.

sentences.zh: 其喪葬，兒女皆七日不食，剔髮而哭，僧尼、道士、親故皆來聚會，音樂送之。

translations.literal: At their funerals sons and daughters all fasted seven days, shaved their heads and wept; monks, nuns, Taoist priests, and kin all came to gather; music sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: At funerals sons and daughters fasted seven days, shaved their heads, and mourned while monks, nuns, Taoist priests, and kin gathered and music accompanied the procession.

sentences.zh: 以五香木燒屍，收灰以金銀瓶盛，送于大水之內。

translations.literal: They burned the corpse with five-fragrance wood, gathered the ashes in gold or silver bottles, and sent them into great waters.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses were burned on five-fragrance wood; the ashes were placed in gold or silver flasks and committed to the open sea.

sentences.zh: 貧者或用瓦，而以彩色畫之。

translations.literal: The poor might use pottery, painted in colors.
translations.idiomatic: The poor used painted earthenware vessels instead.

sentences.zh: 亦有不焚，送屍山中，任野獸食者。

translations.literal: Some also did not burn but sent the corpse into the mountains to let wild beasts eat it.
translations.idiomatic: Some did not burn the body at all but left it in the hills for wild beasts.

sentences.zh: 其國北多山阜，南有水澤，地氣尤熱，無霜雪，饒瘴癘毒蠚。

translations.literal: North of the state were many hills; south were marshes; the climate was especially hot; there was no frost or snow; malarial vapors and poisonous insects abounded.
translations.idiomatic: The north was hilly, the south marshy; the climate was intensely hot, without frost or snow, and thick with malarial miasma and venomous insects.

sentences.zh: 土宜粱稻，少黍粟，果菜與日南、九真相類。

translations.literal: The soil suited millet and rice; there was little broomcorn millet; fruits and vegetables resembled Rinan and Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The soil favored millet and rice rather than broomcorn; fruits and vegetables resembled those of Rinan and Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 異者有婆那娑樹，無花，葉似柿，實似冬瓜；

translations.literal: Among unusual trees was the panasa tree, flowerless, leaves like persimmon, fruit like winter melon;
translations.idiomatic: Among unusual plants was the panasa tree, which bore no flowers, had leaves like persimmon, and fruit like winter melon;

sentences.zh: 菴羅樹，花葉似棗，實似李；

translations.literal: the amra tree, flowers and leaves like jujube, fruit like plum;
translations.idiomatic: the amra tree, whose flowers and leaves resembled jujube and whose fruit resembled plums;

sentences.zh: 毗野樹，花似木瓜，葉似杏，實似楮；

translations.literal: the piye tree, flowers like papaya, leaves like apricot, fruit like paper mulberry;
translations.idiomatic: the piye tree, with blossoms like papaya, leaves like apricot, and fruit like paper mulberry;

sentences.zh: 婆田羅樹，花葉實並似棗而小異；

translations.literal: the potianluo tree, flowers, leaves, and fruit all like jujube but slightly different;
translations.idiomatic: the potianluo tree, whose flowers, leaves, and fruit all resembled jujube with slight differences;

sentences.zh: 歌畢他樹，花似林檎，葉似榆而厚大，實似李，其大如升。

translations.literal: the gebida tree, flowers like crab apple, leaves like elm but thick and large, fruit like plum, as large as a sheng measure.
translations.idiomatic: and the gebida tree, with blossoms like crab apple, thick elm-like leaves, and plum-sized fruit as large as a pint measure.

sentences.zh: 自餘多同九真。

translations.literal: The rest were mostly the same as Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Other produce largely matched that of Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 海中有魚名建同，四足，無鱗，其鼻如象，吸水上噴，高五六十尺。

translations.literal: In the sea was a fish called Jiantong, four-legged, scaleless, its snout like an elephant's; sucking water it spurted upward fifty or sixty zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: The sea held a creature called Jiantong, four-legged and scaleless, with a trunk like an elephant's that sucked up water and spouted it fifty or sixty feet into the air.

sentences.zh: 有浮胡魚，其形似䱉，嘴如鸚鵡，有八足。

translations.literal: There was a Fuhu fish, shaped like a sturgeon, mouth like a parrot's, with eight legs.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Fuhu fish shaped like a sturgeon, with a parrot-like beak and eight legs.

sentences.zh: 多大魚，半身出水，望之如山。

translations.literal: Many great fish, half the body above water, looking from afar like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Enormous fish often surfaced halfway out of the water, looming from a distance like hills.

sentences.zh: 每五六月中，毒氣流行，即以白猪、白牛、白羊於城西門外祠之。

translations.literal: Every fifth or sixth month, when poisonous vapors spread, they sacrificed white pigs, white oxen, and white sheep outside the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth and sixth months, when miasma spread, they sacrificed white pigs, white cattle, and white sheep outside the west gate.

sentences.zh: 不然者，五穀不登，六畜多死，人眾疾疫。

translations.literal: If they did not, the five grains would not ripen, the six livestock would die in great numbers, and the people would suffer epidemic disease.
translations.idiomatic: Without these rites the harvest would fail, livestock would perish, and epidemics would ravage the people.

sentences.zh: 近都有陵伽鉢婆山，上有神祠，每以兵五千人守衞之。

translations.literal: Near the capital was Mount Lingjiabopo, on which stood a spirit shrine, guarded by five thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Near the capital stood Mount Lingjiabopo with a spirit shrine guarded by five thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 城東有神名婆多利，祭用人肉。

translations.literal: East of the city was a spirit named Potuoli, sacrifices using human flesh.
translations.idiomatic: East of the city a spirit named Potuoli received sacrifices of human flesh.

sentences.zh: 其王年別殺人，以夜祀禱，亦有守衞者千人。

translations.literal: The king each year killed people separately, offering night sacrifices and prayers; there were also a thousand guards.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the king executed victims for nocturnal rites, with a thousand guards posted at the shrine.

sentences.zh: 其敬鬼如此。

translations.literal: Their reverence for ghosts was to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was their devotion to spirits.

sentences.zh: 多奉佛法，尤信道士，佛及道士並立像於館。

translations.literal: Many followed the Buddhist law and especially trusted Taoist masters; Buddha and Taoist masters both had images set up in lodges.
translations.idiomatic: They were devout Buddhists who also placed great faith in Taoist masters; images of both were installed in their halls.

sentences.zh: 大業十二年，遣使貢獻，帝禮之甚厚，其後亦絕。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daye they sent envoys with tribute; the emperor treated them very generously; thereafter tribute also ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 12 they sent tribute envoys whom the emperor received with great honor; afterward contact ceased as well.

sentences.zh: 婆利婆利國，自交阯浮海，南過赤土、丹丹，乃至其國。

translations.literal: Bali—The state of Bali: from Jiaozhi by sea, south past Red Earth and Dandan, then reaching its state.
translations.idiomatic: Bali—From Jiaozhi one sailed south past Red Earth and Dandan to reach this kingdom.

sentences.zh: 國界東西四月行，南北四十五日行。

translations.literal: The state's borders were four months' travel east-west, forty-five days north-south.
translations.idiomatic: The realm measured four months' travel east to west and forty-five days north to south.

sentences.zh: 王姓剎利邪伽，名護濫那婆。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Kshatriya; his name Hulannapo.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Kshatriya clan and was named Hulannapo.

sentences.zh: 官曰獨訶邪挐，次曰獨訶氏挐。

translations.literal: Officials were titled Duheyanie, next Duheshanie.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers were titled Duheyanie, with Duheshanie beneath them.

sentences.zh: 國人善投輪刀，其大如鏡，中有竅，外鋒如鋸，遠以投人，無不中。

translations.literal: The people were skilled at throwing wheel-knives, as large as mirrors, with a hole in the center, outer edge sharp like a saw; thrown from afar at people, none missed.
translations.idiomatic: Its people excelled at hurling disc-knives as large as mirrors, pierced at the center with saw-toothed rims that never missed their mark at a distance.

sentences.zh: 其餘兵器與中國略同。

translations.literal: Their remaining weapons were roughly the same as China's.
translations.idiomatic: Their other weapons were much the same as China's.

sentences.zh: 俗類真臘，物產同於林邑。

translations.literal: Customs resembled Zhenla's; products were the same as Linyi's.
translations.idiomatic: Customs resembled Zhenla's and products matched Linyi's.

sentences.zh: 其殺人及盜，截其手，姦者鎖其足，朞年而止。

translations.literal: For murder and theft they cut off the hand; for adultery they shackled the feet, ending after one year.
translations.idiomatic: Murderers and thieves had their hands cut off; adulterers were shackled by the feet for a year.

sentences.zh: 祭祀必以月晦，盤貯酒肴，浮之流水。

translations.literal: Sacrifices were always on the last day of the month; platters held wine and food, floated on flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices were always held on the last day of the month, with platters of food and wine set adrift on the current.

sentences.zh: 每十一月，必設大祭。

translations.literal: Every eleventh month they invariably held a great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Every eleventh month they held a major festival.

sentences.zh: 海出珊瑚。

translations.literal: The sea produced coral.
translations.idiomatic: Coral came from their seas.

sentences.zh: 有鳥名舍利，解人語。

translations.literal: There was a bird named Sheli that understood human speech.
translations.idiomatic: A bird called Sheli could understand human speech.

sentences.zh: 大業十二年，遣使朝貢，後遂絕。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daye they sent envoys to court with tribute; afterward it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 12 they sent tribute envoys; contact ceased thereafter.

sentences.zh: 于時南荒有丹丹、盤盤二國，亦來貢方物，其風俗物產，大抵相類云。

translations.literal: At that time in the southern wilds the two states Dandan and Panpan also came to offer local products; their customs and products were generally similar, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the southern realms of Dandan and Panpan also sent native goods; their customs and products were said to be much the same.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：禮云：「南方曰蠻，有不火食者矣。」

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Rites state: "The south is called Man; there are those who do not eat by fire.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: The Book of Rites says, "The south is called the land of the Man, where some peoples do not cook their food with fire.

sentences.zh: 書稱：「蠻夷猾夏。」

translations.literal: The Documents state: "The Man and Yi are unruly toward Xia."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents declares, "The barbarians of the four quarters harass the central lands."

sentences.zh: 詩曰：「蠢爾蠻荊。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "You foolish Man of Jing."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "You foolish barbarians of Jing."

sentences.zh: 種類實繁，代為紛梗。

translations.literal: Their kinds are truly numerous; generation after generation they have been a source of turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribes are indeed numerous, and age after age they have stirred disorder.

sentences.zh: 自秦并二楚，漢平百越，地窮丹徼，景極日南，水陸可居，咸為郡縣。

translations.literal: From Qin annexing the two Chu, Han pacifying the Hundred Yue, the land reaching the cinnabar frontier, the view extending to Rinan—all places habitable by water or land were made commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qin conquest of Chu and the Han pacification of the Hundred Yue, the frontier ran to the Vermilion March and the horizon to Rinan; every habitable coast and river valley was organized into commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 暨乎境分吳、蜀，時經晉、宋，道有污隆，服叛不一。

translations.literal: Down to when the realm was divided between Wu and Shu, through the Jin and Song periods, the Way had its rises and falls, submission and rebellion never uniform.
translations.idiomatic: When the land was split between Wu and Shu and through the Jin and Song eras, fortunes rose and fell and allegiance shifted without end.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，克平九宇，煬帝纂業，威加八荒。

translations.literal: Gaozu received the Mandate and conquered the nine realms; Emperor Yang succeeded to the enterprise and extended awe to the eight wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu received Heaven's mandate and pacified the nine realms; Emperor Yang succeeded him and extended imperial might to the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 甘心遠夷，志求珍異，故師出於流求，兵加於林邑，威振殊俗，過於秦、漢遠矣。

translations.literal: He set his heart on distant barbarians and sought rare and strange things; thus armies went forth to Liuqiu, troops were applied to Linyi, awe shook alien customs—far surpassing Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: He bent his will toward distant peoples and coveted exotic treasures, dispatching armies to Liuqiu and troops against Linyi until foreign realms trembled at Sui might—a reach that far exceeded Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 雖有荒外之功，無救域中之敗。

translations.literal: Although there were achievements in the wild beyond, they could not rescue defeat within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: For all their triumphs beyond the frontier, they could not stave off catastrophe at the heart of the empire.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「非聖人，外寧必內憂。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "If one is not a sage, external peace necessarily brings internal worry.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, "When the ruler is no sage, peace abroad is sure to breed trouble within.

sentences.zh: 誠哉斯言也！

translations.literal: How true indeed are these words!
translations.idiomatic: How true indeed that saying proves!
